Create a set of Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Ionicons or Lucide Markers

Source: R/magicIcons.R
magicIcons.Rd

This function is intended as a more up-to-date implementation of leaflet::awesomeIcons(). Key benefits include having access to modern Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Ionicons and Lucide icons, and allowing any colour to be used for the marker and icon.

Usage

magicIcons(
  icon = "circle",
  markerColor = leaf.magic::awesomePalette$blue,
  iconColor = "auto",
  marker = "marker",
  markerSize = 30L,
  outlineColor = NULL,
  outlineWidth = NULL,
  library = "fontawesome",
  className = NULL,
  dir = tempdir(),
  shadow = TRUE
)

Arguments

icon

Name of the icon. A full list of available icons can be found using fontawesome::fa_metadata(), https://icons.getbootstrap.com/, https://ionic.io/ionicons or https://lucide.dev/icons/, depending on library. When library = "text", the text (or numbers) to show in each marker instead, and when library = "svg", a string of SVG markup.

markerColor

The color of the marker. Not used when marker = "none".

iconColor

The color of the icon. "auto" chooses black or white for each marker, whichever has the greater contrast with markerColor. When marker = "none", "auto" instead gives the icon the colour markerColor, as there is no marker for it to contrast with.

marker

The shape of the marker. Defaults to "marker", which uses the standard teardrop shaped pin, similar to leaflet::addMarkers(). The other built-in shapes are:

  • Pointed shapes, which sit on their location with their tip: "marker-square" (a pin with a square head) and "callout" (a speech bubble).

  • Shapes centred on their location: "circle", "square", "diamond", "triangle", "hexagon", "star" and "heart".

  • "none", which removes the marker entirely and places the icon directly on the map.

Custom shapes can be created using markerShape(). marker may be a character vector of shape names, a single markerShape(), or a list of markerShape()s and/or shape names to use a different shape for each marker.

markerSize

The width of the marker in pixels. Defaults to 30, which is roughly the same size as leaflet::addMarkers().

outlineColor

The colour of the outline around each marker. Defaults to a slightly darker shade of markerColor. A contrasting colour (e.g., "white") helps markers stand out against similarly coloured basemaps.

outlineWidth

The width of the outline in pixels. Defaults to a subtle outline which scales with markerSize (around half a pixel at the default size). Markers are not shrunk to make room for wider outlines, so they grow by the extra width.

library

One of "fontawesome", "bootstrap", "ionicons", or "lucide" defining the icon library of interest. Defaults to "fontawesome". Alternatively, "text" shows icon as text, which is useful for numbered or lettered markers (e.g., icon = 1:10). Text is bold and shrinks to fit, so is best kept to around three characters. "svg" uses icon as raw SVG markup (e.g., '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">...</svg>'), so any icon can be used. Parts of the SVG which use currentColor or have no fill of their own take on iconColor. Only use SVG markup you trust, as it is inserted directly into legends.

className

a custom class name to assign to both icon and shadow images

dir

The directory in which markers are saved. By default this is tempdir(), which is deleted at the end of each R session. Providing an alternative directory will allow markers to persist between R sessions. dir is created if it does not already exist.

shadow

Should markers have a shadow? Defaults to TRUE. As with the default leaflet::addMarkers() marker, pointed shapes such as "marker" cast a shadow up and to the right, while other shapes have a soft shadow just beneath them. "none" never has a shadow. The shadow of a custom shape is set using the shadow argument of markerShape().

Value

a leaflet::iconList(), to be passed to the icon argument of leaflet::addMarkers(). If any argument is a formula, a formula which builds that leaflet::iconList() from the layer's data is returned instead.

Details

Each marker is built as a single SVG image, with the icon nested inside of the marker shape, and saved to dir. As markers are vector images, they stay sharp at any markerSize and on high resolution screens. Markers are only built once for each combination of icon, colours, marker shape and library, so you may find the use of magicIcons() speeds up the more you use it in a single session.

Each icon library is provided by a separate package which must be installed to use it: {fontawesome}, {bsicons} or {lucidr}. Ionicons are downloaded from https://unpkg.com the first time each icon is used in a session, so require an internet connection.

Using formulas

As with leaflet::awesomeIcons(), icon, markerColor, iconColor, marker, markerSize, outlineColor and outlineWidth may be one-sided formulas (e.g., ~site_type), which are evaluated against the data of the layer the markers are added to. Markers are then built when the layer is added, so magicIcons() must be passed directly to the icon argument of leaflet::addMarkers(). Formulas and constants can be mixed freely, and formulas may call other functions, such as an iconFactor() scale or a leaflet::colorFactor() palette (e.g., markerColor = ~pal(site_type)).

See also

markerShape(), addIconLegend(), iconFactor(), iconBin(), iconQuantile()

Author

Jack Davison

Examples

# create map
library(leaflet)
port_talbot |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    icon = dplyr::recode_values(
      site_type,
      "Urban Industrial" ~ "industry",
      "Urban Traffic" ~ "car",
      "Urban Background" ~ "city",
      default = "x"
    ),
    color = dplyr::recode_values(
      site_type,
      "Urban Industrial" ~ "#12436D",
      "Urban Traffic" ~ "#801650",
      "Urban Background" ~ "#28A197",
      default = "#3D3D3DFF"
    )
  ) |>
  leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    icon = magicIcons(icon = ~icon, markerColor = ~color, iconColor = "white"),
    lat = ~latitude,
    lng = ~longitude,
    popup = ~site
  )
